issues.title: P0 security: qualify full-chain post-quantum trust, W1 proof, mining economics and recovery
issues.body:
## Security determination — 2026-10-31

**Whole-chain post-quantum security is NOT qualified**. No source-only test, ML-DSA primitive conformance, STARK label, or successful launch script may promote `production_consensus_activation` or `PQ-128`.

Related staged implementation:
- #627 hardens classical Ed25519 authenticated session creation under PQ account settings (Draft; Rust execution not observed).
- #628 adds explicit negative whole-chain PQ claim guard, 12 adversarial fixtures, and six-domain acceptance matrix (Draft; isolated Python fixtures only).

### P0: acceptance obligations / independently falsifiable exit conditions

- [ ] **Trust-root inventory and downgrade resistance.** Inventory *every effect-authorizing entry point* (transaction/accounts, keys/nonce, task sources/evaluators, operator, governance/release, Hepta admission and cross-repository FinalUse, Cell provider discovery, recovery, light clients and software upgrades) with source/function/production reachability, authority pin, signed domain, revocation and last-use recheck. In PQ-only profiles, classical-only authentication must be rejected, not used as OR fallback. Keep classical research artifacts explicitly isolated. Separate signing authentication from semantic authorization.
- [ ] **W1 PQ-128 proof security.** Freeze precise relation, guest/compiler/backend hashes, hash commitments, quantum Fiat–Shamir model, FRI soundness, composition/recursion, circuit and worst-case invalid-verification cost. Independently establish target PQ security. Existing RISC Zero 3.0 published 96/99-bit component estimates and Groth16 do not establish the desired whole-chain PQ-128.
- [ ] **Quantum mining/chain selection.** Model **complete legal W1** work per attempt: witness material, reversible oracle, uncomputation, challenge/setup amortization, quantum memory, power/time/success probability, actual proof production, propagation and reorg. Compare cheapest legitimate classical/quantum adversaries with frozen equal-cost hardware assumptions. Stress current retarget window/factor, timestamp manipulation, stale blocks, selfish mining and cumulative-work selection. Record threat-model bounds rather than unproven unconditional quantum hardness.
- [ ] **Pre-exposure PQ ownership and no-rollback.** Bind PQ claims *before* classical compromise can counterfeit migration. Native migration must retain old nonce floors, liabilities, key generation, evidence and fork/reorg semantics; secure dual possession at migration when meaningful. Define external monotonic anchor / recovery policy for total self-consistent database rollback. Cold crash/power-loss, old/new key, branch conflict and replica divergence negatives required.
- [ ] **Actual wire/network/cost acceptance.** Evaluate 3,309-byte ML-DSA-65 signature and full NPQ6 authenticated tx vs legacy 2,048-byte ceiling; test valid/invalid bounded verification CPU, queueing, spam-amplification, memory RSS, disk/WAL, bandwidth, p95/p99 and reorg on target hosts; no arbitrary cap lift.
- [ ] **Independent end-to-end authorization and activation.** Pin SHA/toolchain/dependencies, rerun preflight, full Rust test/Clippy/format, source-integrity negatives, independent cryptographic/security review, WAN/eclipsing/fault tests, auditable release governance, separately verified public chain work. Activation remains explicit and false until every above gate is accepted by its proper authority.

### Evidence ledger format

For each gate, retain exact commit SHA, affected source entries/identity format, frozen threat model, positive/negative attack cases, independent verifier/test implementation, exact commands and environment, raw outcomes including failures, reviewer, residual assumptions and rejection criteria. Do **not** mark this issue complete based on a checklist alone. Preserve current mainline and existing project boundary: no force-push, self-approval or activation.

The immediate focus is source-level authorization reachability and real NPQ6 integration; quantum W1 and proof system require separate cryptographic research and independent qualifications.

issues.title: P0: retain native 4s signed confirmation under 16 hostile W1 producers
issues.body:
## Exact P0 evidence — native business completion fails under hostile W1 calls
**HOLD / NO PRODUCTION ACTIVATION / not a claim of PQ-128.** Captured from exact tested candidate SHA `4aee60b75d87b974b1d82bd1694d2eb3159c29fd` in [required baseline run 41182805121](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/actions/runs/41182805121) `protocol-contract` job 124483513589, native artifact [head-protocol-contract](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/actions/runs/41182805121/artifacts/13035259479), paths `from-zero-native/confirmation/report.json`, `from-zero-native/manifest.json`, and `from-zero-native-host/systemd-run.log`.

**This is not a systemd setup failure.** The reviewed unit was installed, source build/preparation succeeded, Host errors were empty, and all five named native Rust tests ran and passed with exit code 0. The aggregate original business gate correctly failed with `CONFIRMATION_TARGET`, so native service exit=1. Do not reclassify passing individual tests as meeting the actual deadline/concurrency requirement.

### Paired original, unchanged four-second window
- Attack-free: seven signed honest submissions finish at ~208 ms; independent cross-node history/replay and six-block-deep transaction confirmation finish at ~2,681 ms, with `client_confirmed_transactions=1` and `finite_business_target_met=true`.
- 16 from-zero attackers: seven signed submissions still accepted but finish at ~1,462 ms. Three History queries were accepted at ~1,561, 2,859 and 3,660 ms; the native replay/confirmation path reported `PUBLIC_REQUEST_DEADLINE` and did **not** produce independent confirmation before 4,000 ms. `client_confirmed_transactions=0`, `finite_business_target_met=false`, `full_native_state_equal=false`. No invalid W1 attack was accepted.
- Under pressure service metrics: `work_started=300`, `work_finished=300`, `executor_refusals=293`, `queue_backpressure_events=619`, `pending_grant_wait_ns=18520483411` cumulative across waiters, `queue_wait_ns=4159440905` cumulative, `mutation_cpu_charged_ns=495619251`, `abandoned_tasks=3`, `mutation_cpu_clock_failures=0`. Those aggregate wait times are NOT single-request p99 or physical CPU hardness.
- No pressure callback or threshold may be removed; passing the original five named tests is *insufficient*.

### Required closure
1. Preserve original source, native W1 validation, independent client re-execution, 4s business deadline, 16 attacker workers, CPU/cgroup budgets, packet bytes, signed transaction, and false-trace rejection. No artificial prioritization by identity, no widening/refill, no new grace period, no bypassed proof/state verification.
2. Trace time from signed submits → original per-connection admission/grant queue → durable state/W1 validation → History response → independent page-by-page native replay → final chainwork/confirmation; capture per-stage wall and CPU with complete samples, including failures.
3. Fix **actual** fair scheduling / expensive validation or independently verified replay costs without violating producer-neutral PoN semantics. Show resource-weighted net benefit and counterexamples against malicious adaptation.
4. Repeat exact original test and prospective-merge native job on pinned hardware. Require both baseline and pressure confirmation **inside original window**; compare p95/p99, RSS, CPU, queue pressure, invalid full-replay costs, end-to-end signed business.
5. Only after reproducible CI and independent adversarial review close this issue. Does **not** establish network TPS, absolute physical work hardness, quantum security, or public WAN fairness.

Parent blocker: #629. The narrow Clippy blocker was separately addressed by [Draft #638](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/pull/638), which cannot solve this runtime failure.
